https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide to a few popular IP‑lookup APIs that return **company‑level data** (organization name, domain, contact details, etc.) when you supply an IP address. All of them expose a simple HTTP GET endpoint that you can hit from any language (Python, JavaScript, curl, Postman, etc.). | Service | Key Features | Free Tier | Typical Endpoint | Example | |---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|---------| | **ipinfo.io** | • Organization name, ASN, domain
• Contact email & phone (if available)
• Rich metadata (city, region, postal, timezone) | 50 k requests/month (no key needed for basic data) | `https://ipinfo.io//json` | `https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json` | | **ipstack.com** | • Company name, domain, phone, email
• Geo‑location, carrier, threat score | 10 k requests/month (API key required) | `https://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=YOUR_KEY` | `https://api.ipstack.com/8.8.8.8?access_key=12345` | | **ipapi.co** | • Organization, domain, phone, email
• Geo‑data, threat level | 30 k requests/month (API key optional for higher limits) | `https://ipapi.co//json/` | `https://ipapi.co/8.8.8.8/json/` | | **ipgeolocation.io** | • Company, domain, phone, email, website
• Geo‑data, threat score | 30 k requests/month (API key required) | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=` | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=12345&ip=8.8.8.8` | | **ipwhois.io** | • Organization, domain, phone, email
• Geo‑data, threat score | 10 k requests/month (API key required) | `https://ipwhois.app/json/` | `https://ipwhois.app/json/8.8.8.8` | --- ## How to Use One of These APIs Below is a **Python** example that demonstrates how to call the **ipinfo.io** endpoint and parse the JSON response. Feel free to adapt the snippet to any of the other services by swapping the URL and adding an API key if required. ```python import requests def get_company_info(ip_address: str): """ Query ipinfo.io for company data associated with an IP address. Returns a dictionary with organization, domain, phone, email, etc. """ url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip_address}/json" try: resp = requests.get(url, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() except requests.RequestException as e: print(f"Error querying ipinfo.io: {e}") return None data = resp.json() # ipinfo.io returns the following keys that are relevant to company data: # - org: Organization name (e.g., "AS15169 Google LLC") # - hostname: Domain name (e.g., "dns.google") # - city, region, country, postal, timezone, loc, etc. # - For paid plans, you may also get "phone" and "email" under "org" or "contact" company_info = { "organization": data.get("org"), "domain": data.get("hostname"), "city": data.get("city"), "region": data.get("region"), "country": data.get("country"), "postal": data.get("postal"), "timezone": data.get("timezone"), "latitude": data.get("loc", "").split(",")[0] if data.get("loc") else None, "longitude": data.get("loc", "").split(",")[1] if data.get("loc") else None, # ipinfo.io does not expose phone/email in the free tier; you need a paid plan. } return company_info if __name__ == "__main__": ip = "8.8.8.8" info = get_company_info(ip) print(info) ``` ### Switching to a Paid Plan (e.g., ipstack) If you need **contact email/phone** that the free tier does not expose, you can upgrade to a paid plan and add the API key: ```python def get_company_info_ipstack(ip_address: str, api_key: str): url = f"https://api.ipstack.com/{ip_address}" params = {"access_key": api_key} resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() data = resp.json() return { "organization": data.get("organization"), "domain": data.get("domain"), "phone": data.get("phone"), "email": data.get("email"), # ... other fields ... } ``` --- ## Things to Keep in Mind | Topic | Notes | |-------|-------| | **Rate Limits** | Free tiers usually cap at 10–50 k requests/month. If you exceed, you’ll get HTTP 429. | | **Privacy** | Some IPs belong to private networks or VPNs; the returned data may be incomplete or generic. | | **Accuracy** | The “company” field often contains the ISP or hosting provider, not necessarily the end‑user’s business. | | **Legal** | Always check the terms of service. Some providers restrict commercial use or require attribution. | | **Caching** | IP ownership rarely changes; cache responses for 24–48 h to reduce API calls. | --- ## Quick Test (curl) ```bash # ipinfo.io (free) curl -s https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json | jq . # ipstack (requires key) curl -s "https://api.ipstack.com/8.8.8.8?access_key=YOUR_KEY" | jq . ``` --- ### Bottom Line - **ipinfo.io** is the easiest to start with (no key for basic data). - For richer contact details (phone, email), upgrade to a paid plan on **ipstack**, **ipapi.co**, or **ipgeolocation.io**. - All services expose a simple JSON endpoint; just plug the IP into the URL and parse the response. Happy coding! If you need help wiring this into a specific stack (Node.js, Go, etc.) or setting up caching, let me know.
